description:
## Unblocked by `write-primitives-architecture-fixes` (2026-05-04)

`WriteOperationType.AGGREGATE_PERSIST` and `AGGREGATE_MERGE` landed
with `DataFrameWriteCapabilities.supports_aggregate_persist` /
`supports_aggregate_merge` flags and dispatch methods
(`execute_aggregate_persist` / `execute_aggregate_merge`) that accept
caller-supplied callables for the engine-specific sketch chain. PySpark
presets enable both flags. The implementation pattern documented in the
architecture-fixes TODO matches w2-w3 below: the consumer closes over
the spark session + source data + group cols inside the builder
callable; the manager owns timing/durability/result-envelope.

w1 (research spike) is now obsolete since the framework decision is
made — proceed directly to w2 (HLL persist+merge), w3 (top-K, Spark 4.1+
guarded), w4 (docs), w5 (changelog).

## Original description

The merged write_primitives sketch category exposes the persist +
merge + requery loop only on the SQL surface (8 ops). PySpark is
the only DataFrame engine in BenchBox's matrix with a comparable
DataFrame-side sketch API:

- `pyspark.sql.functions.hll_sketch_agg(col)` (Spark 3.5+) — builds
  DataSketches HLL state, returns BINARY column.
- `pyspark.sql.functions.hll_union_agg(col)` — merges HLL states.
- `pyspark.sql.functions.hll_sketch_estimate(col)` — extracts count.
- `pyspark.sql.functions.approx_top_k_accumulate(col)` (Spark 4.1+)
  + `_combine` + `_estimate` — same triplet for top-K.
- `percentile_approx(col, p)` for KLL-equivalent (no separate
  accumulate/combine triplet at the DataFrame layer).

This TODO adds a Spark-only DataFrame implementation of the sketch
ops, mirroring the SQL category's structure. It does NOT extend the
cross-engine matrix — Polars / DataFusion / Pandas / Modin / cuDF /
Dask have no DataFrame-layer sketch persistence today.

Captured as a deferred item from the post-merge expansion review and
the DataFrame approximate-aggregates research (TODO #121's deferred
list).

anti_patterns.dont: add KLL DataFrame ops in this TODO
anti_patterns.why: Spark's KLL surface is SQL-UDAF-only today and a DataFrame chain would need to fall back to percentile_approx (which is one-shot, defeats the persist+merge story)

anti_patterns.dont: crash on Spark < 4.1 when top-K ops are invoked
anti_patterns.instead: runtime-guard with a version check and skip cleanly with a logged reason.
anti_patterns.why: the BenchBox PySpark adapter is documented to support Spark 3.5+

anti_patterns.dont: extend BenchBox's DataFrame execution model beyond what dataframe_operations.py already supports
anti_patterns.instead: surface the need to the user before extending.
anti_patterns.why: that's a structural change with broader scope implications

anti_patterns.dont: mirror the 8 SQL sketch ops 1-for-1 in DataFrame mode
anti_patterns.instead: express each persist+merge cycle as its own DataFrame chain and document the mapping in w4 docs, not in op IDs.
anti_patterns.why: the DataFrame fluent-API idiom doesn't match the SQL CTE idiom (e.g. CREATE TABLE + INSERT + SELECT in one op)

deferrals.reason: Spark exposes percentile_approx as a one-shot aggregate but no DataFrame-layer accumulate/combine/estimate triplet for KLL. Wait until kll_sketch_agg ships at the DataFrame layer (currently SQL-UDAF-only via DataSketches Spark integration).
deferrals.resolved_reason: [G4 sweep] conditional-unmet: operations.yaml shows kll_sketch_agg is still SQL-catalog-only; no DataFrame-layer KLL surface has shipped yet.

deferrals.reason: Storage-size methodology is being added in `write-primitives-sketch-clickhouse-and-storage-metrics` for the SQL surface. Once that lands, mirror it for the DataFrame surface — but do that as a follow-up, not in this TODO.
deferrals.summary: DataFrame-side storage-size validation for sketch persistence

preserves.behavior: All existing 117 SQL write_primitives operations execute identically — DataFrame additions are net-new and do not touch the SQL catalog.
PySpark adapter remains usable on Spark < 4.1 (top-K ops skip cleanly).

verifications.expected: all tests pass, including new test_dataframe_sketch_ops.py

verifications.description: PySpark live: HLL persist+merge DataFrame ops execute end-to-end
verifications.expected: op completes; merged distinct estimate within tolerance bounds

verifications.command: uv run -- benchbox run --platform pyspark --benchmark write_primitives --scale 0.01 --queries sketch_df_topk_accumulate_combine
verifications.description: Top-K ops skip cleanly on Spark < 4.1 (if local Spark is older)
verifications.expected: either passes (Spark 4.1+) or skips with a clear 'requires Spark 4.1+' log message — no crash

work_units.notes:
Build a DataFrame-side equivalent of `sketch_query_theta_union_merge`:
  - groupBy(date, region).agg(F.hll_sketch_agg("l_orderkey"))
    to produce per-partition HLL sketches in a BINARY column.
  - Persist (Delta or Parquet) — measure write latency.
  - Read back, merge with F.hll_union_agg, estimate with
    F.hll_sketch_estimate — measure merge+requery latency.
Include in the result_contract a tolerance-bounded distinct
count (re-tune empirically against PySpark; HLL++ vs DataSketches
HLL produce different bias).
work_units.summary: Add PySpark dataframe_operations for HLL persist + merge (mirrors sketch_query_theta_union_merge)

work_units.notes:
Mirror `sketch_query_topk_combine` using
F.approx_top_k_accumulate("l_shipmode") /

Runtime guard: if PySpark version < 4.1, skip the op cleanly with
an informative log message (do NOT raise) — the SQL sibling
handles this via platform_overrides; the DataFrame side needs an
equivalent check at op load time or at first-call.
